    Track 4 · Advanced · Lesson 9

    Observability and drift in production

    After this lesson you can explain how the RunEvent spine makes a pipeline observable, what drift detection does, and how to decide when a production model needs retraining.

    Level: advanced Read time: ~9 min Prerequisites: Serving and inference optimization

    A deployed model meets inputs you never trained on, and the world it learned keeps moving. Observability is how you notice when it stops being good — before your users do.

    The RunEvent spine, recapped

    From Track 3: every stage emits a RunEvent via emit_event() — a reason code from a lint-gated taxonomy plus a severity (info / warning / error / critical). One stream feeds every observability surface: the run-event timeline and failure clusters on Ship → Monitor, the audit explorer, and the support bundle. The emission is best-effort (wrapped in try/except at each call site), so a bug in observability can never break the actual data or training path. That single design choice is what makes the whole pipeline debuggable after the fact.

    Drift: quality decays quietly

    A model that scored 0.93 at launch can be 0.80 six months later without anyone touching it — because the inputs drifted. New slang, new product names, a new kind of customer. This is drift, and it's invisible unless you measure for it.

    Drift detection: re-run the gold set on the live model

    BrewSLM's Ship → Deploy stage (Track 3) has a drift check on every served version: it re-runs your gold set — the answer key under Data → Labels — against the deployed model and compares the pass rate to the baseline recorded at training time. You supply the live model's predictions — bring your own inference client and paste them into the check's form (the API and CLI can also call an endpoint URL themselves) — and run it on whatever cadence you choose; nothing schedules it for you. A significant drop emits deployment_drift_detected — the same gold set you built in Track 1, now a production sensor.

    # drift check — Ship → Deploy → a served version → "Run drift check"
re-run the answer key vs the deployed model
  launch:  accuracy 0.93
  today:   accuracy 0.86   → drift!  emit deployment_drift_detected
# also: deployment_smoke_failed (promote-time), deployment_promote_blocked

    Your gold set keeps working

    The gold set you curated for evaluation (the answer key) doesn't retire at launch — it becomes the regression sensor that watches the live model for as long as you keep running the check. That's a big payoff for the work you put into it in Track 1.

    When to retrain

    Drift detection tells you that quality dropped; deciding what to do is judgment:

    • Drift detected → gather recent real inputs, add them (via the review queue under Data → Generate → Details), re-split on Data → Split, re-train, re-evaluate against the same pass/fail rules on Results → Verdict. The Track 3 loop, triggered by a signal instead of a hunch.
    • New failure clusters (Ship → Monitor, or Results → Failures for eval misses) → a targeted data fix (augment_from_cluster), not a full retrain.
    • Stable → leave it alone. Retraining a healthy model just risks regressions.

    Key idea

    The RunEvent spine makes every stage observable; best-effort emission means observability never breaks the data path. Drift detection re-runs your gold set (the answer key) against the deployed model on a cadence you choose, turning it into a production sensor — and a drop is the signal to gather fresh data and retrain through the same pass/fail rules.

    Key terms

    observability
    The ability to see what the pipeline did and how the live model is performing.
    RunEvent spine
    The one event stream every stage emits to, feeding all monitoring surfaces; best-effort so it can't break the data path.
    drift
    Production quality decay caused by input distributions changing over time.
    drift detection
    A re-run of the gold set (answer key) against the deployed model, compared with the training baseline, to catch quality drops. In BrewSLM: Ship → Deploy → Run drift check.
    support bundle
    A consumer of the RunEvent stream packaging the events/state needed to debug an issue.
    retrain trigger
    Using a drift signal or new failure clusters to decide when to gather data and retrain.
